value.reason: server.ts:670 registers GET /rest/memories with only utils.asyncHandler(getMemories()). Unlike the negative example, which uses security.isAuthorized(), the Evidence shows no authorization middleware on this route. The handler in routes/memory.ts:24 calls MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) without an attributes allow-list. Line 25 then sends the result straight to the client with res.json({ status: 'success', data: memories }). So every Memory record is returned with its full associated User object. Per models/user.ts, that object includes email, username, the hashed password (security.hash(clearTextPassword)), lastLoginIp, profileImage and other redacted fields that look like secrets or tokens. No toJSON override, defaultScope or attribute exclusion appears in the Evidence. The route matches the positive example almost exactly: an anonymous public endpoint serialises the whole user model, exposing credential hashes and personal data to anyone. This is broken object property level authorization and a failure to control access to personal data.
